task.description: WF-02 Step 2d hard gate on REQ-038's implementation: idiomatic OTP/Elixir usage, design-doc fidelity, promotion_review_store.ex edit consistency, and an explicit REVIEWER call on the event-append-after-commit tradeoff SECURITY-REVIEWER flagged for this step per the design doc's OQ-3.
acceptance_criteria: Idiomatic Elixir check: @spec/@type coverage, pattern-matching style vs. activate/2, FOR UPDATE locking idiom vs. activate_draft/2, 5-helper decomposition assessed for over-fragmentation

Code independently spot-checked against the design doc's transaction boundary, 3-guard-case ordering, status-enum mapping, and cardinality-branching lookup -- not trusted from ELIXIR-DEV's/SECURITY-REVIEWER's summaries
promotion_review_store.ex edit checked for documentation consistency across ASCII diagram, bullet list, and prose
Explicit REVIEWER opinion given on the event-append-after-commit tradeoff, not just acknowledgment
Scope creep check: confirm only the two declared files were touched

result.summary:
Read lib/letflow/definitions.ex's new rollback_definition_version/4 plus its 5 private helpers (do_rollback/6, run_rollback_transaction/4, swap_active_pointer/3, finish_rollback/8, supersede_matching_review/4) directly, alongside promotion_review_store.ex's supersede_review/3 widening, the design doc (lib/letflow/design/req038-promotion-rollback.md), promotion.ex (the OQ-1 precedent), and docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md. Confirmed git diff main...HEAD touches exactly lib/letflow/definitions.ex and lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex among application code (plus the design doc and workflow handoffs, which are correctly-committed artefacts, not scope creep) -- no scope creep.

Idiomatic Elixir/OTP: PASS, no crutches found. This is pure functional/DB-transactional code with no process involved (correct per design and per every REQ-030/031/036/037 sibling in this module) -- gen_statem/supervision questions are not applicable here, as the design itself states. @spec/@type coverage matches the module's own established convention: the public function has both; the 5 private helpers have neither, which mirrors this same file's pre-existing precedent (run_activate_transaction/4, activate_draft/2, interpret_activate_result/1 are also un-@spec'd) rather than a new gap. Pattern-matching/control-flow style is idiomatic and, in one respect, better-adapted than a literal copy of promote_definition/3's shape would have been: rollback_definition_version/4 uses a plain if/else for its single permission_checker boolean check, where promote_definition/3 uses cond do because it has two sequential guard conditions -- using if for exactly one condition is the more idiomatic choice, and ELIXIR-DEV adapted the pattern rather than mechanically copying cond syntax for a single boolean. The FOR UPDATE locking idiom (lock("FOR UPDATE") |> Repo.all, generalized from activate/2's single-row Repo.one) is the same idiom, correctly generalized to a whole-row-set lock. The three guard cases inside run_rollback_transaction/4 use cond do with is_nil/==/true, appropriate given the guard needs to test two independent conditions across two different in-memory values (current_active, target_row) rather than pattern-match one struct's fields the way run_activate_transaction/4's case does -- a reasonable, not gratuitous, divergence forced by the different shape of this problem. The 5-helper decomposition is well-factored, not over-fragmented: each helper's name and boundary map 1:1 onto the design doc's own step numbering (Step 2/TX1 -> run_rollback_transaction/4, Step 2e -> swap_active_pointer/3, Step 3-5 -> finish_rollback/8, Step 4's sub-lookup -> supersede_matching_review/4), which aids traceability rather than adding indirection for its own sake.

One pattern worth watching, flagged per this gate's own 'worth watching as it grows' framing rather than as a defect: finish_rollback/8 takes 8 positional scalar parameters. This is not a new problem REQ-038 introduces -- promotion.ex's append_promotion_event/9 already has 9 -- but it is now the second instance of a growing positional-parameter list standing in for what could eventually be a small context struct, in the same submodule family. Not asking for a rework (matching the existing, already-accepted precedent, and inventing a new struct type here would itself be exactly the kind of ahead-of-need abstraction this gate is supposed to flag against), but worth a note if a third instance appears.

Design-doc fidelity: PASS, verified directly against the code, not the design doc's own claims or prior agents' summaries. Transaction boundary: run_rollback_transaction/4's Repo.transaction/1 wraps exactly steps 2a-2e (the lock, the three guards, and swap_active_pointer/3's two Repo.update_all calls) -- confirmed swap_active_pointer/3 is called from inside the transaction fn, not after it. do_rollback/6 wraps only that call in try/rescue (matching the design's explicit 'Exception safety' note that Steps 3/4 are never folded into :transaction_failed). finish_rollback/8 (event-append + supersede lookup) runs strictly after the transaction returns, confirmed by code structure (called from the `with` clause following `transaction_result`), matching the design's deliberate divergence from R-Co's literal single-transaction framing. Guard-case ordering: cond do checks is_nil(current_active) -> :process_key_not_found, then current_active.version == target_version -> :already_active, then (in the true branch) the target-row lookup -> :version_never_active if nil -- exactly the design's Step 2b/2c/2d order. Status-enum mapping: target_row lookup filters status in [:active, :deprecated], excluding :archived, matching design section 3's SUPERSEDED->:deprecated mapping and INV-RB-4 exactly. Cardinality-branching lookup: supersede_matching_review/4's case on matching_reviews has exactly the three branches design section 6 specifies ([] -> nil, [single_review] -> supersede-then-id-or-nil-on-race, [_, _ | _] -> nil with zero Repo calls in that branch) -- confirmed the ambiguous branch contains no mutation, matching INV-RB-10 and the Rework-1 fix it exists to enforce.

promotion_review_store.ex edit -- idiom/consistency angle: PARTIAL credit, one real finding (non-blocking). The bullet list (`supersede_review/3` -- `[:applied, :approved, :failed, :rejected]`) and the prose paragraph explaining why :approved is a genuine, needed edge (the promote_definition/3-vs-mark_review_applied/2 window) are both cleanly and consistently updated, as is supersede_review/3's own @doc. The ASCII diagram, however, is not cleanly redrawn -- it reuses the pre-existing diagram's backslash/pipe structure with a minimal patch and then relies on a prose footnote immediately below it ('The middle diagonal out of [approved] (labeled implicitly above, since ASCII space is tight) is supersede_review/3 called directly on an :approved row') to explain what the diagram itself does not make visually clear. The design doc's own item 2 asked for 'adding the new approved -> superseded arrow to its own ASCII diagram' -- what was delivered functions more as an ambiguous mid-diagram insertion requiring the reader to already trust the footnote than a self-evident new arrow. This does feel bolted-on rather than cleanly integrated, called out explicitly per this gate's own question rather than waved through. Not a blocker: the substantive information is present and correct in the bullet list, prose, and @doc, so no reader is actually misled, only the diagram's own visual-clarity purpose is diminished. Recommend a follow-up redraw (not urgent enough to block this gate) the next time this file is touched.

Event-append-after-commit tradeoff (the explicit REVIEWER call SECURITY-REVIEWER's issue asked for): reviewed promotion.ex's OQ-1 handling directly (moduledoc lines 26-44, already-accepted at REQ-036/037's own Step 2d) and compared it to rollback_definition_version/4's identical structural shape (TX1 commits the pointer swap; opts[:event_appender] is called after, never nested inside the transaction). My call: the underlying engineering decision is sound and should NOT be reworked now -- nesting an arbitrary caller-injected closure's I/O inside an open Ecto transaction would require trusting that closure to compose correctly with a transaction it doesn't own, which is a real, general reason to keep this ordering, not merely a copy-paste of precedent. However, I do not think this is fully equivalent risk to promote_definition/3's case, and I want that stated explicitly rather than silently inherited as settled: rollback is disproportionately likely to be invoked during incident response, exactly the scenario where 'the pointer swap happened but no audit event exists' is most costly to discover after the fact, and unlike promotion's flow there is no second bookkeeping call (comparable to mark_review_applied/2) whose own failure would independently surface a mismatch for a rollback. The mitigating factor that makes this acceptable today: this function already propagates opts[:event_appender]'s {:error, reason} synchronously as its own return value rather than swallowing it, so a caller that checks its return value does learn about the gap immediately, and there is still no real event_appender implementation wired into any orchestrator to test a stronger guarantee against (same deferred-wiring gap promotion.ex already discloses). Building a stronger guarantee now (e.g. an outbox/pending-event marker row inside TX1) would need a new migration REQ-038's own scope explicitly excludes, and would be exactly the kind of framework machinery a stage hasn't reached yet that this gate exists to flag against building prematurely. Verdict: ACCEPT the tradeoff for REQ-038 as implemented, matching the promote_definition/3 precedent -- but flag explicitly (issues below) that when a real event_appender/orchestrator wiring lands for rollback specifically, it should treat a post-swap append failure with elevated urgency (retry/alert) rather than being satisfied with the same handling routine promotion uses, given rollback's audit trail is disproportionately likely to matter exactly when it's missing.

Type-safety gap worth noting per this gate's standing brief (not a defect, not blocking): rollback_result()'s superseded_review_id: Ecto.UUID.t() | nil collapses two semantically distinct cases (zero matching promotion_reviews rows -- nothing needed superseding -- vs. more than one ambiguous match -- something needed superseding but this design safely declined to guess) into the same nil value. A sum type distinguishing these (e.g. a 3-way result instead of a nilable UUID) would let a future consumer of this result tell the two cases apart at compile time instead of needing to re-query promotion_reviews to find out which case occurred; Elixir's type system doesn't surface this distinction today, only the design doc's own prose does (design section 6, already disclosed there as an accepted, schema-constrained limitation, not new to this review). Also noting, for the same standing reason: opts[:permission_checker]/opts[:event_appender] being Keyword.fetch!/2'd (KeyError only at call time if omitted) is the third instance of this same shape in this codebase (PromotionPlan, promotion.ex, now definitions.ex) -- a language with mandatory record fields would catch an omitted hook at compile time instead of at first invocation. Both are pre-existing, deliberate, already-disclosed tradeoffs (design section 4.1/4.2, section 6/OQ-5) that this design correctly inherits rather than invents; noted per the standing brief's 'note it, even if not asked' instruction, not as new findings requiring rework.

Decision-record consistency: PASS. tenant_id is derived from opts[:prefix] via TenantProvisioning.tenant_id_for_schema_name/1 and never accepted as a separate argument -- rollback_definition_version/4's signature has no tenant_id parameter at all, matching docs/migration/decisions/0003-ecto-schema-strategy.md's 2026-08-17 addendum (derivation from the resolved schema, never a caller-supplied value) exactly, and matching this same module's own established convention for every other function. Schema-per-tenant via :prefix-scoped Repo calls is used throughout, consistent with Decision B. No framework/library choice in this diff contradicts any decision record.

Scope creep: PASS, none found. git diff main...HEAD --stat confirms only lib/letflow/definitions.ex and lib/letflow/definitions/promotion_review_store.ex were touched among application code; the design doc and prior-step handoff files are correctly-committed workflow artefacts per core-directives.md's File Placement Rules, not scope creep.

Incidental finding, out of REQ-038's scope, filed rather than fixed here per core-directives.md's 'No Issue Left Local-Only': promotion_review_store.ex's moduledoc opening paragraph (untouched by this diff, confirmed via git diff) lists this module's six transition functions with stale arities that don't match any real function (e.g. states insert_review/1, actual is insert_review/2; states supersede_review/2, actual is supersede_review/3) -- pre-existing since REQ-035/037, not introduced by REQ-038, not blocking this gate. Filed as docs/issues/ISS-0038.yaml and GitHub issue #127.

issues.description: promotion_review_store.ex's moduledoc ASCII diagram for the widened 7->8 edge set is not cleanly redrawn -- it patches the pre-existing diagram's backslash/pipe structure minimally and relies on a prose footnote ('labeled implicitly above, since ASCII space is tight') to explain the new approved->superseded edge, rather than a self-evident new arrow as the design doc's section 7 item 2 asked for. The bullet list, prose paragraph, and supersede_review/3's own @doc are all cleanly and correctly updated -- only the diagram itself feels bolted-on. Not blocking (no reader is misled, only the diagram's visual-clarity purpose is diminished); recommend a redraw next time this file is touched.

Explicit REVIEWER call on the event-append-after-commit tradeoff (design doc OQ-3, carried forward by SECURITY-REVIEWER's step-02c issue[0]): the architectural pattern (commit TX1 first, call the injected event_appender after, never nested) is sound and correctly reused from promote_definition/3 -- not asking for rework now, and not a violation of anything. However, this is NOT fully equivalent risk to promotion's case: rollback is disproportionately likely to be invoked during incident response, exactly when a missing audit event for an already-committed pointer swap is most costly to discover, and rollback has no analogous second bookkeeping call (comparable to mark_review_applied/2) whose own failure would independently surface the gap. The current mitigation -- opts[:event_appender]'s {:error, reason} is propagated synchronously as this function's own return value, not swallowed -- is the correct minimum given no real event_appender/orchestrator wiring exists yet to build a stronger guarantee against. Recommend: when a real orchestrator eventually wires event_appender for rollback specifically (a future requirement, not REQ-038), it should treat a post-swap append failure with elevated urgency (retry/alert) rather than inheriting promotion's routine handling unmodified, given rollback's audit trail matters disproportionately exactly when it's missing.

Incidental, out-of-scope finding: promotion_review_store.ex's moduledoc opening paragraph (untouched by REQ-038's diff, pre-existing since REQ-035/037) lists the module's six transition functions with arities that don't match any function actually defined in the file (only approve_review/4 is correct; insert_review/2, reject_review/3, mark_review_applied/2, mark_review_failed/2, supersede_review/3 are all stated one arity lower). Filed as docs/issues/ISS-0038.yaml and GitHub issue #127 per core-directives.md's No Issue Left Local-Only rather than fixed here -- not blocking this gate, not introduced by this diff.
